Every protein is tested in nine contrasts between the six group-by-time means (HR and LR at T1, T2
and T3), and in two F-tests that ask about the whole trajectory. The fit is limpa's `dpcDE()`,
which carries each value's standard error into a precision weight. This step also gives the
whole-proteome view: a PCA and PERMANOVA per time point.

## Packages

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
library(here)
library(limma)
library(limpa)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "workbooks.R"))
inputs <- c(
  proteins = "01_Processing/02_Quantification/c_data/proteins.rds",
  corrected = "01_Processing/03_Blood_Correction/c_data/proteins_corrected.rds"
)
paths <- vapply(inputs, here, character(1))
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))
```

## Input

limpa's protein values with standard errors, and the biopsy table with the blood index.

```{r}
#| label: input
proteins <- readRDS(paths[["proteins"]])
meta <- as_tibble(proteins$targets)
count(meta, group, timepoint)
```

## Design and fit

The design has one mean per group and time point (`group_time`) plus the blood index as a
covariate, so every comparison is made at equal blood content. Each person gave three biopsies,
so person is a block: limma estimates how alike one person's biopsies are and uses it in every
test. `sample.weights = TRUE` gives each biopsy a weight from how noisy it is, so the three thin
biopsies count less in these fits without being dropped. Only `dpcDE()` fits use the weights;
the PCA and PERMANOVA below, and every later method without a model, use all biopsies equally.

```{r}
#| label: fit
design <- model.matrix(~ 0 + group_time + blood, meta)
colnames(design) <- sub("^group_time", "", colnames(design))
fit <- dpcDE(proteins, design, block = meta$subject, sample.weights = TRUE, plot = FALSE)
c(within_person_correlation = round(fit$correlation, 3))
```

## Sample weights

A weight above 1 means the biopsy fits the model better than average. The weights must not differ
by group, or they would tilt the HR-against-LR comparison.

```{r}
#| label: weights
sample_weights <- meta |>
  select(sample_id, subject, group, timepoint) |>
  mutate(weight = fit$targets$sample.weight)
arrange(sample_weights, weight) |> head(4)
weight_test <- wilcox.test(weight ~ group, data = sample_weights, exact = FALSE)
c(median_hr = median(sample_weights$weight[sample_weights$group == "HR"]),
  median_lr = median(sample_weights$weight[sample_weights$group == "LR"]),
  wilcoxon_p = weight_test$p.value)
stopifnot(weight_test$p.value > 0.05)
```

## Nine contrasts

| Contrast | Compares | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `Training_HR`, `Training_LR` | T2 − T1 within the group | descriptive |
| `Acute_HR`, `Acute_LR` | T3 − T2 within the group | descriptive |
| `Baseline_HRvLR` | HR − LR at T1 | baseline reference |
| `Trained_HRvLR`, `Acute_HRvLR` | HR − LR at T2, at T3 | descriptive |
| `Training_Interaction` | HR's training change minus LR's | primary |
| `Acute_Interaction` | HR's bout change minus LR's | secondary |

The groups come from an outcome, so the T1 difference shows how far apart the split starts.

```{r}
#| label: contrasts
contrast_matrix <- makeContrasts(
  Training_HR = HR_T2 - HR_T1, Training_LR = LR_T2 - LR_T1,
  Acute_HR = HR_T3 - HR_T2, Acute_LR = LR_T3 - LR_T2,
  Baseline_HRvLR = HR_T1 - LR_T1, Trained_HRvLR = HR_T2 - LR_T2, Acute_HRvLR = HR_T3 - LR_T3,
  Training_Interaction = (HR_T2 - HR_T1) - (LR_T2 - LR_T1),
  Acute_Interaction = (HR_T3 - HR_T2) - (LR_T3 - LR_T2),
  levels = design
)
roles <- tibble(
  contrast = colnames(contrast_matrix),
  role = case_when(
    contrast == "Training_Interaction" ~ "primary",
    contrast == "Acute_Interaction" ~ "secondary",
    contrast == "Baseline_HRvLR" ~ "baseline_reference",
    TRUE ~ "descriptive"
  )
)
eb <- eBayes(contrasts.fit(fit, contrast_matrix), robust = TRUE)
```

## Results per protein and contrast

`topTable()` gives each protein's logFC with its 95% interval, moderated t and p; `fdr` is
Benjamini-Hochberg within the contrast. Π = p^|logFC| (Xiao et al. 2014) is the nominal call:
small when p is small and the fold change large; Π < 0.05 counts as a hit beside logFC, interval,
p and FDR.

```{r}
#| label: results
annotation <- tibble(
  uniprot_id = rownames(proteins), gene = sub(";.*", "", proteins$genes$Genes),
  n_observed = rowSums(proteins$other$n.observations > 0)
)
results <- map(set_names(colnames(contrast_matrix)), \(contrast) {
  topTable(eb, coef = contrast, number = Inf, sort.by = "none", confint = TRUE) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(logFC, logFC_lower = CI.L, logFC_upper = CI.R, t, p = P.Value, fdr = adj.P.Val) |>
    bind_cols(annotation, x = _)
}) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "contrast") |>
  mutate(pi_score = p^abs(logFC), sig_pi = sign(logFC) * (pi_score < 0.05))
contrast_summary <- results |>
  summarise(
    n_tested = n(), pi_up = sum(sig_pi == 1), pi_down = sum(sig_pi == -1),
    n_nominal = sum(p < 0.05), n_fdr_05 = sum(fdr < 0.05), min_fdr = min(fdr), .by = contrast
  ) |>
  left_join(roles, by = "contrast")
contrast_summary
```

Chance alone puts about `r round(nrow(proteins) / 20)` proteins below p = 0.05 in each contrast.

## Trajectory F-tests

An F-test asks about several contrasts at once and returns one p per protein, with no direction.
"Any difference" asks whether HR and LR differ at T1, T2 or T3; "shape" asks whether the two
groups' training and bout changes differ (both interactions). The contrasts above say where and in
which direction.

```{r}
#| label: f-tests
f_test <- \(coefs) {
  topTable(eb, coef = coefs, number = Inf, sort.by = "none") |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(f = .data$F, p = P.Value, fdr = adj.P.Val) |>
    bind_cols(annotation, x = _)
}
trajectory_tests <- bind_rows(
  any_difference = f_test(c("Baseline_HRvLR", "Trained_HRvLR", "Acute_HRvLR")),
  shape = f_test(c("Training_Interaction", "Acute_Interaction")),
  .id = "test"
)
trajectory_tests |>
  summarise(n_nominal = sum(p < 0.05), n_fdr_05 = sum(fdr < 0.05), min_fdr = min(fdr), .by = test)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-p-histogram
#| fig-cap: "p values per contrast. Dashed: a flat null (tested / 20)."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6
results |>
  mutate(contrast = factor(contrast, colnames(contrast_matrix))) |>
  ggplot(aes(p)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, boundary = 0, fill = "grey35") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = nrow(proteins) / 20, linetype = 2, colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~contrast) +
  labs(x = "p", y = "proteins") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9)
```

A spike at zero on a flat background is signal; a flat histogram is chance.

## Does one group's response carry over to the other?

The proteins one group changes with training (or the bout) at Π < 0.05 or p < 0.05 form a set; fry
(limma) tests that set in the other group's contrast. Sets need 5 or
more proteins. Beside each test: the set's mean logFC in the group that chose it (inflated by the
selection) and in the other group, and the share of members with the same sign. fry is a rotation
test across biopsies that keeps the person block and its within-person correlation.

```{r}
#| label: fry
pairings <- tribble(
  ~set_from, ~ranked_on,
  "Training_HR", "Training_LR", "Training_LR", "Training_HR",
  "Acute_HR", "Acute_LR", "Acute_LR", "Acute_HR"
)
signature <- \(contrast, criterion, direction) {
  r <- filter(results, .data$contrast == .env$contrast)
  hit <- if (criterion == "pi") r$pi_score < 0.05 else r$p < 0.05
  hit & if (direction == "up") r$logFC > 0 else r$logFC < 0
}
fry_concordance <- pmap(pairings, \(set_from, ranked_on) {
  sets <- expand_grid(criterion = c("pi", "nominal"), direction = c("up", "down")) |>
    mutate(set = paste(criterion, direction, sep = "_")) |>
    mutate(rows = pmap(list(criterion, direction), \(c, d) which(signature(set_from, c, d))))
  sets <- filter(sets, lengths(rows) >= 5)
  own <- filter(results, contrast == set_from)$logFC
  other <- filter(results, contrast == ranked_on)$logFC
  carried <- transmute(sets, set,
    mean_logfc_own = map_dbl(rows, \(i) mean(own[i])),
    mean_logfc_other = map_dbl(rows, \(i) mean(other[i])),
    same_sign_share = map_dbl(rows, \(i) mean(sign(own[i]) == sign(other[i])))
  )
  fry(fit$EList, index = set_names(sets$rows, sets$set), design = design,
    contrast = contrast_matrix[, ranked_on], block = meta$subject, correlation = fit$correlation
  ) |>
    as_tibble(rownames = "set") |>
    transmute(
      set_from, ranked_on, set, n_proteins = NGenes, direction = Direction, p = PValue, fdr = FDR
    ) |>
    left_join(carried, by = "set")
}) |>
  list_rbind()
fry_concordance
```

## Whole-proteome structure per time point

A PCA on the blood-corrected values (proteins scaled) at each time point, and PERMANOVA (vegan's
`adonis2()`, 9,999 permutations) asking how much of the distance between people group explains
(R²) at that time point. Time is also tested across all biopsies, with permutations kept inside
each person; the model has no person term, so this test is conservative.

```{r}
#| label: pca
corrected <- readRDS(paths[["corrected"]])
scaled_at <- \(rows) scale(t(corrected$E[, rows]))
pca_by_time <- map(set_names(c("T1", "T2", "T3")), \(tp) {
  rows <- meta$timepoint == tp
  pca <- prcomp(scaled_at(rows))
  as_tibble(pca$x[, 1:2], rownames = "sample_id") |>
    mutate(pc1_share = summary(pca)$importance[2, 1], pc2_share = summary(pca)$importance[2, 2])
}) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "timepoint") |>
  left_join(select(meta, sample_id, subject, group), by = "sample_id")
permanova <- \(rows, term, blocks = NULL) {
  set.seed(1)
  control <- permute::how(nperm = 9999, blocks = blocks)
  fit <- vegan::adonis2(dist(scaled_at(rows)) ~ ., data = meta[rows, term], permutations = control)
  tibble(n_samples = sum(rows), r2 = fit$R2[1], f = fit$F[1], p = fit$`Pr(>F)`[1])
}
permanova_tests <- bind_rows(
  map(set_names(c("T1", "T2", "T3")), \(tp) permanova(meta$timepoint == tp, "group")) |>
    list_rbind(names_to = "window") |>
    mutate(term = "group", .before = 1),
  permanova(rep(TRUE, nrow(meta)), "timepoint", blocks = factor(meta$subject)) |>
    mutate(term = "time", window = "all", .before = 1)
)
permanova_tests
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-pca
#| fig-cap: "Biopsies per time point on PC1 and PC2 of the blood-corrected values."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.2
ggplot(pca_by_time, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~timepoint, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(HR = "#D6404E", LR = "#7F7F7F"), name = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9)
```

## Validation

```{r}
#| label: validate
stopifnot(
  nrow(results) == nrow(proteins) * ncol(contrast_matrix), !anyNA(results$p),
  all(results$fdr >= results$p),
  all(results$logFC_lower <= results$logFC & results$logFC <= results$logFC_upper),
  nrow(trajectory_tests) == 2 * nrow(proteins)
)
```

## Summary

`r nrow(proteins)` proteins in nine contrasts: `r sum(contrast_summary$n_fdr_05)` calls at BH < 0.05
in all, and between `r min(contrast_summary$n_nominal)` and `r max(contrast_summary$n_nominal)` at
p < 0.05 per contrast against about `r round(nrow(proteins) / 20)` by chance. Group explains
`r round(100 * permanova_tests$r2[1], 1)`%, `r round(100 * permanova_tests$r2[2], 1)`% and
`r round(100 * permanova_tests$r2[3], 1)`% of the distance between people at T1, T2 and T3.

## Save

`fit.rds` holds the fit, the moderated contrasts, the design and contrast matrix; later steps read
it.

```{r}
#| label: save
out <- here("02_HRvLR", "01_Protein_Contrasts", "c_data")
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(
  list(fit = fit, eb = eb, design = design, contrast_matrix = contrast_matrix, roles = roles),
  file.path(out, "fit.rds")
)
write_workbook(
  list(
    protein_by_contrast = arrange(results, match(contrast, colnames(contrast_matrix)), p),
    contrast_summary = contrast_summary,
    trajectory_tests = arrange(trajectory_tests, test, p),
    sample_weights = sample_weights,
    fry_concordance = fry_concordance,
    pca_by_time = pca_by_time,
    permanova = permanova_tests
  ),
  c(
    "Per contrast and protein: logFC with 95% CI, t, p, FDR (BH within contrast), Π, the Π call.",
    "Per contrast: tested, Π up and down, p < 0.05 and BH < 0.05 counts, lowest FDR, role.",
    "Per protein: moderated F for any HR-LR difference and trajectory shape; FDR (BH) within test.",
    "Per biopsy: limpa sample weight; tested HR against LR.",
    "fry: each group's responders tested in the other group's contrast; FDR within each pairing.",
    "PC1 and PC2 per biopsy within each time point, blood-corrected values, proteins scaled.",
    "PERMANOVA: group at each time point; time across all biopsies within person."
  ),
  file.path(out, "protein_contrasts.xlsx"), inputs, paths
)
```
